title: PersonaClaims struct exists and is tested, but service.rs hand-rolls a divergent json! instead
description:
persona-core/src/hvid.rs:8-35 defines PersonaClaims and PresenceInfo — documented as 'Serialises to the exact JSON shape required by the spec', derives Serialize/Deserialize, exported from lib.rs:15, and covered by two round-trip tests.

Nothing in the codebase ever constructs them outside those tests (verified by grep: the only hits are hvid.rs and the lib.rs re-export). The one place that actually emits the persona extension object, persona-grpc/src/service.rs:162-173, builds it by hand with serde_json::json!.

What goes wrong — the two have already diverged, silently:
- PresenceInfo::attested_at and ::present_until are declared `String` and documented 'RFC 3339 timestamp' (hvid.rs:14, hvid.rs:16). service.rs:169-170 emits them as u64 Unix seconds.
- PersonaClaims::identity_assurance is `IdentityAssurance` with #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]. service.rs:165 emits `claim.assurance.to_string()` — same wire text today only because Display and the serde rename happen to agree; nothing enforces that.

So the struct that claims to define the spec shape does not describe what the daemon actually emits, and the hvid.rs tests pass while asserting nothing about the shipping output. A reader trusting hvid.rs writes a consumer that fails to deserialize a real token.

Rewrite: build the value in service.rs as a PersonaClaims and serialize it (`serde_json::to_value(&claims)`), picking one representation for the timestamps and making PresenceInfo match. That deletes the hand-rolled json! literal and makes the existing hvid.rs tests actually guard the wire format. If Unix seconds are the intended format, change PresenceInfo's fields to u64 and fix its doc comments.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.51 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
